question.text: If the plane $3 x+y+2 z+6=0$ is parallel to the line $\frac{3 x-1}{2 b}=3-y=\frac{z-1}{a}$, then the value of $3 a+3 b$ is

solution.text:
Given plane $3 x+y+2 z+6=0$
and line $\frac{x-\frac{1}{3}}{\frac{2 b}{3}}=\frac{y-3}{-1}=\frac{z-1}{a}$
Since, plane is parallel to line, then
$$
\begin{aligned}
& 3\left(\frac{2 b}{3}\right)+(1)(-1)+2(a)=0 \\
& 2 b-1+2 a=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad a+b=\frac{1}{2} \\
&
\end{aligned}
$$
Now, $3 a+3 b=\frac{3}{2}$
